annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Numerical verification rests on an invalid proof method.
× Cannot conclude proof from a single numerical case.

teacherNote: To prove a trigonometric identity, you must prove it holds for all angles A using standard trigonometric identities (such as 1 - cos²A = sin²A and cosec A = 1/sin A). Verifying the equality for an arbitrary specific angle like 30° is only a numerical check, not a valid general proof. This method does not work in general, so the working built on it cannot earn method marks — use a method that holds in every case.

rubric.point: Using the Pythagorean trigonometric identity 1 - cos²A = sin²A
